Who we are
The City of Salisbury is the most progressive council in South Australia, driving growth, jobs, housing and opportunity in the north. With a workforce of over 400 people, we offer the chance to collaborate with teams across the organisation to deliver meaningful, community-focused projects.
The City Infrastructure Department delivers asset management, capital works, and maintenance programs, as well as oversees lease management for local community and sporting clubs, and security and civil compliance functions.
Join us and see the positive impact your work can make.
About the role
The City of Salisbury is seeking three experienced Asset Engineers to join the Engineering Assets & Systems team within City Infrastructure. Opportunities are available across Civil, Roads and Drainage asset portfolios.
Reporting to the Divisional Head, Engineering Assets & Systems (Asset Engineer - Civil and Asset Engineer - Roads) or the Senior Stormwater Engineer (Asset Engineer - Drainage), you will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving asset management plans, undertaking engineering investigations and modelling, and supporting long-term infrastructure planning and investment decisions.
You will play a key role in managing and improving some of the City's most important infrastructure assets, including roads, drainage networks, wetlands, bridges, boardwalks, coastal assets, carparks, signage and stormwater infrastructure, helping ensure they continue to meet the needs of our growing community.
Your key responsibilities will include
- Develop, maintain and improve Asset Management Plans across a range of infrastructure asset classes.
- Undertake engineering investigations, modelling, analysis and reporting to support asset management decisions.
- Develop capital renewal, maintenance and lifecycle programs.
- Assess asset condition, risk, service levels and long-term investment priorities.
- Prepare project briefs and business cases for infrastructure projects and renewal programs.
- Evaluate consultant reports, designs and technical proposals.
- Provide specialist engineering and asset management advice across the organisation.
- Support planning for future growth and infrastructure needs across the city.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community members, developers, government agencies, service authorities and internal stakeholders.
- Communicate technical information and asset management recommendations clearly to a diverse range of stakeholders, including residents, elected members and senior leaders.
- Respond to enquiries from residents, elected members and other stakeholders.
About you
You are a qualified engineer with experience in infrastructure asset management and a passion for delivering practical, long-term outcomes for communities. You combine strong technical capability with excellent communication skills and can confidently engage with a wide range of stakeholders. You are able to translate complex engineering and asset management information into clear, practical advice that supports informed decision-making.
You will also have
- Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, equivalent qualifications, or proven extensive experience in asset management relating to civil infrastructure and stormwater.
- Experience in infrastructure asset management, planning and lifecycle analysis.
- Knowledge of asset management frameworks such as ISO 55000 and IIMM/IPWEA practices.
- Experience using asset management, GIS and engineering modelling systems.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Proven experience building productive relationships with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong written communication skills, including the preparation of reports, business cases and technical documentation.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Current driver's licence.
Desirable
- Postgraduate qualifications in asset management.
- Experience working within local government.
What we offer
- State-of-the-art Salisbury Community Hub is 25 minutes from the CBD with excellent rail and road connections.
- Modern and positive work environments.
- Free car parking.
- Flexible work options.
- Three additional leave days per year.
- Annual pay rises.
- Health and wellbeing programs, including skin checks, health assessments, flu vaccinations and an employee assistance program.
- Professional development opportunities.

About the Role
PCP Solutions is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Graduate Civil Engineer to join our growing team.
This is an excellent opportunity for a recent engineering graduate or someone in the early stages of their career to gain valuable hands-on experience working on large-scale civil infrastructure projects.
Working alongside experienced Project Managers, Site Engineers and Supervisors, you will assist with the planning, coordination, quality assurance and delivery of civil construction works from commencement through to completion.
The successful applicant will be provided with ongoing guidance and support while developing their technical knowledge, project management skills and practical understanding of civil construction operations.
The Company
PCP Solutions is a leading civil earthworks and commercial plumbing business based in Toowoomba, delivering projects across South East Queensland.
With over 70 staff, PCP Solutions specialises in large-scale infrastructure works for Tier 1 contractors whilst maintaining a supportive, family-focused culture.
We pride ourselves on delivering quality projects, building strong working relationships and providing opportunities for our employees to grow and develop within the business.
Key Responsibilities
Working under the guidance of senior project personnel, your responsibilities will include:
- Assist with daily site inspections and monitoring construction activities.
- Prepare, maintain and complete Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and associated quality assurance documentation.
- Assist with the preparation and submission of project reports and documentation to Principal Contractors.
- Support daily work front reporting, progress tracking and construction records.
- Assist with project programming, scheduling and monitoring critical deadlines.
- Provide project administration and engineering support to Project Managers, Site Engineers, Supervisors and Quality and Safety personnel.
- Assist with reviewing construction drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Monitor supplier material conformance and ensure materials meet project specifications.
- Assist with quantity calculations, material take-offs and procurement requirements.
- Support the implementation and maintenance of project quality, workplace health and safety and environmental controls.
- Assist with identifying and reporting potential project risks, delays and construction issues.
- Maintain accurate project records, filing systems and document control processes.
- Provide regular project progress updates to the Project Manager and wider project team.
- Ensure compliance with the company's Integrated Management System (IMS), policies and procedures.
Skills and Qualifications
We are looking for someone who is eager to learn, takes initiative and is passionate about developing a career in civil construction.
The successful applicant will ideally possess:
- A completed Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
- Recent graduates and applicants with up to 2 years of industry experience are encouraged to apply.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work professionally with clients, suppliers, subcontractors and site personnel.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate documentation.
- A willingness to learn and develop practical construction and project management skills.
- Basic understanding of civil construction methods, engineering drawings and specifications.
- Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- Ability to work independently when required and contribute positively to a team environment.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a strong commitment to workplace safety.
- A current driver's licence and Construction White Card, or willingness to obtain a White Card prior to commencing.
- Willingness to travel to regional project locations as required.
Previous experience in civil construction, earthworks, water infrastructure or quality assurance will be highly regarded but is not essential.
What We Offer
- Opportunity to gain hands-on experience on major civil infrastructure projects.
- Mentoring and ongoing support from experienced engineering and construction professionals.
- Exposure to Tier 1 construction projects and industry-leading systems.
- Career development and progression opportunities within a growing company.
- A supportive, family-focused team environment.
- Competitive remuneration based on qualifications and experience.
- A diverse role offering both site-based and project administration experience.
How to Apply
If you are a motivated Graduate Civil Engineer looking to kick-start your career and gain practical experience in the civil construction industry, we would love to hear from you.
Apply via SEEK or email your resume and cover letter to admin@pcpsolutions.com.au
Join PCP Solutions and build your engineering career with a team committed to quality, safety and delivering successful projects.

Company Overview
Noble Built is an Adelaide-based residential construction and property development company specialising in custom home design and construction, residential property development, knockdown and rebuild projects, land subdivision and investment builds. Working closely with project management team, the role will involve preparing engineering drawings based on design requirements and technical specifications, incorporating drawing revisions and ensuring documentation complies with relevant Australian Standards, building codes and local council requirements. 8.           Liaising with civil engineer and project supervisor regarding technical drawings, design revisions and construction requirements.

- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience as a Civil Engineering Draftsperson, preferably within the residential construction or property development industry.

- Sound knowledge of civil engineering drawings, technical specifications, site layouts, earthworks, stormwater drainage and other civil infrastructure works.

Be part of a growing business with ongoing residential construction and development projects.

candidates.content_text:
Our client is one of Australia's largest contractors with a focus a major Defence infrastructure projects.
 They are looking for Site/Project Engineers to join the team on a FIFO basis from Perth
 The project
 The $200m+ package covers a broad civil scope, including pavements, tank works, FRP, earthworks and drainage. It’s a chance to build your civil experience across several disciplines on a high-profile Defence project.
 The role
 As a Project Engineer, you’ll coordinate the engineering and day-to-day delivery of these packages, working closely with the Senior Project Engineer, Project Manager and wider site team. You’ll be involved in:
 - Planning and programme requirements
 - Subcontractor coordination
 - Quality management
 - Technical queries and RFIs
 What’s on offer
 - 2&1 FIFO roster
 - 20% uplift
 - Flights, Accom, Meals covered 
 - Exposure to a large-scale Defence project and a broad mix of civil packages
 - Pathway to Senior Project Engineer on a project of this size
 About you
 - Civil construction experience as a Site OR Project Engineer or similar
 - Experience in general civil scope: earthworks, drainage, tank works or FRP (not all are essential)
 - Strong communication and subcontractor coordination skills
 - Must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident
 - Must be able to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance
 Apply
 For a confidential chat, contact Scott at Verra on 0413 889 442 or sgowling@verra.com.au

candidates.content_text:
- Maximum Term, Part-Time position for 21 hours per week
 - Exposure to a diverse portfolio of community infrastructure projects
 - A collaborative and supportive workplace culture
The City of Canada Bay is a thriving, colourful community, surrounded by the beautiful bays of Sydney Harbour. The area is also known for its parklands, cycle paths and walkways. City of Canada Bay Council’s values underpin how we operate: 
We act with integrity| We empower our people| We are respectful| We work together| We innovate.
Kick-start your career in project management and make a real impact in your community.
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Graduate Project Officer to join our team and support the delivery of Council's Capital Works Program. This is an exciting opportunity for a recent graduate looking to develop project management skills while contributing to a diverse range of community-focused infrastructure projects.
About the role
As a Graduate Project Officer, you will assist in managing and delivering a variety of capital works projects, that could include:
 - Playgrounds and open space improvements
 - Sports field upgrades
 - Building construction and renewals
 - Asset renewal programs
 - Civil engineering and infrastructure projects
 - Other community and public domain improvement projects
Working alongside experienced project professionals, you will gain hands-on experience across all stages of the project lifecycle while developing the skills, knowledge and capabilities required for a successful career in project management and contract administration.
Key Responsibilities:
 - Assist in the planning, coordination and delivery of assigned projects within Council's Capital Works Program. 
 - Support project managers to ensure projects are delivered in accordance with approved scope, budget, quality standards and timeframes. 
 - Contribute to project initiation activities, procurement processes, stakeholder engagement and contract administration. 
 - Monitor project progress, prepare reports and maintain project documentation. 
 - Liaise with contractors, consultants, stakeholders and internal teams to support successful project outcomes. 
 - Assist with project handover and closure activities to ensure a seamless transition to asset owners and operational teams. 
 - Demonstrate a customer-focused and service-oriented approach throughout all stages of project delivery.
About the Person
To be successful in this position, you will have:
 - A recent graduate (or final year graduate) with a bachelor’s degree in a construction related field such as Civil Engineering, Building and Construction, or a related discipline with demonstrated progress towards completion of such qualifications. 
 - Strong organisational and problem-solving skills. 
 - A collaborative approach and willingness to learn. 
 - An interest in infrastructure, community facilities and capital works delivery. 
 - The ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively within a team environment.
 - Current Class “C” Drivers Licence
 - Workcover accredited Construction Induction (White) Card preferred
What’s on offer
We are offering a remuneration between $79,533 to $91,463 per annum plus Super (pro-rata basis 3-days/week).
The City of Canada Bay also offers excellent employee benefits which include:
 - A range of flexible work arrangements including hybrid work from home arrangements
 - A supportive, energetic, and passionate team
 - Significant leave benefits 
 - Continuous training, support, and leadership development
 - Health and Wellbeing programs (Yoga classes, Fitness Passport, Flu vaccinations, Skin Cancer Checks)
 - And much, much more!
Want to know more?
Further information regarding the requirements of this role can be found in the attached Position Description, alternatively for a confidential discussion please contact Michael Isaac, Coordinator Projects on 02 9911 6425 or email Michael.Isaac@canadabay.nsw.gov.au  
To learn more about working at City of Canada Bay Council, please click the link below.
How to apply
Candidates MUST apply online. Applications close at 11:30pm, 22 November and will not be accepted through any other medium.
If you have any accessibility requirements, please feel free to contact Grace Aberin on 02 9121 0238  or email  grace.aberin@canadabay.nsw.gov.au   to discuss.
The City of Canada Bay Council is a Child Safe Organisation that recognises and advocates for the rights of Children and Young People and are committed to a Safe Workplace. 
The City of Canada Bay Council is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer committed to maintaining, growing and supporting a diverse, respectful, collaborative & inclusive workplace. We welcome and encourage applications from diverse community groups and ages including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, LGBTIQA+, people with disabilities, and other diversity groups. 
 Formal offers of employment are subject to standard Council pre-employment checks including medical and other background checks.

candidates.content_text:
AWCON is a rapidly growing Australian civil construction contractor delivering complex projects across the mining and heavy industry sectors. With a proven track record delivering projects valued from $1M to $100M+, we partner with Tier 1 clients on major projects throughout Australia.
With offices and projects spanning every state of Australia, AWCON offers the opportunity to build a long-term career working on diverse and challenging projects across the country.
With a strong pipeline of upcoming works and continued national growth, we are seeking applications from high-performing Project Engineers to join the team across multiple projects
The Opportunity
Working closely with Project Managers and site teams, you will play a key role in coordinating project activities, managing technical and compliance requirements, and supporting efficient project delivery on site.
You’ll be embedded in complex surface and underground construction projects, taking ownership of planning, coordination and execution across FRP, concrete and associated civil works.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
- Driving project delivery safely, on time and on budget
- Working closely with Project Managers and Supervisors to optimise sequencing and productivity
- Providing technical problem solving and support on site
- Managing documentation, QA and compliance without losing sight of delivery
- Coordinating subcontractors, crews, materials and project resources
- Building strong relationships with clients, subcontractors and stakeholders
- Identifying smarter, faster and more efficient ways to deliver work
What We’re Looking For 
A Project Engineer who is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and has genuine project delivery experience across underground construction, FRP and concrete works.
You’ll bring:
- A Civil or Structural Engineering degree
- 5+ years’ experience in project engineering, with a strong background in underground construction
- Demonstrated experience delivering FRP and concrete works
- Practical knowledge of construction methodology, sequencing and project delivery
- The ability to coordinate multiple work fronts and keep projects moving
- Strong technical, planning and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working closely with Supervisors, crews, subcontractors, clients and Project Managers
- A strong understanding of safety, quality, QA and compliance requirements
- The ability to work autonomously, make decisions and take ownership of your work
- Experience working on remote or FIFO mining projects
Ready to Join the Team?
If you're an experienced Project Engineer with underground construction, FRP and concrete experience and you're looking for your next opportunity with a growing Australian company that values safety, teamwork and quality, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply now via SEEK.
AWCON is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourages applications from people of all backgrounds.
Note – successful applicants will be required to complete a pre-employment medical, drug and alcohol screening and police clearance.

candidates.content_text:
Cadet Designer
Requisition Number: 1400
Salary Range: $64,175.57 - $86,649.77 per annum
Position Type: Full Time Maximum Term for up to 6 Years
Cadet Position – This position is intended for up to a 6-year maximum term to allow for 2 years of bonded service to Council post-graduation.
Location: Council Chambers, 119-145 Spence Street, Cairns
Application Close Date: Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 11.30pm AEST
Kick-start your career in Civil Design with one of the region’s largest and most diverse infrastructure portfolios!
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Cadet Designer to join our Design & Survey Services team. This is an exciting opportunity to earn while you learn, gain hands-on industry experience, and build a rewarding career in civil engineering and infrastructure design.
Our Ideal Candidate:
We are seeking a Cadet Designer who is eager to learn and willing to dedicate themselves to continuous development within a technically focused environment. The ideal candidate will have completed Year 12 or hold a Certificate III in Engineering and be qualified for acceptance into an Associate Degree in Engineering (Civil) course, or an equivalent qualification. They will demonstrate a detail-oriented mindset, strong analytical skills, and a willingness to integrate into and contribute positively to the established team culture. A current "C" Class Driver's Licence is required, with the ability to independently drive between business locations to meet operational needs. The successful candidate will also maintain a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes for the Cairns community.
What You’ll Be Doing:
- Undertake training in the use of civil design software (AutoCAD, 12d Model and relevant GIS systems).
- Undertake training in the investigation, planning, development and delivery of civil design projects.
- Develop knowledge and understanding of relevant standards, guidelines and legislative documents (e.g. Austroads, Queensland Urban Drainage Manual, Queensland Streets, Main Roads technical publications and Australian Standards).
- Assist with field investigations, traffic surveys and stakeholder consultation associated with allocated projects.
- Preparation of detailed civil design drawings and estimates for a range of multi-disciplinary infrastructure projects with guidance and as directed.
- Provide general administrative assistance such as database maintenance and document control using established procedures.
- Develop an approach to contributing technical knowledge and innovative problem solutions to design activities.
Study Allowances
Council provides paid study and examination leave, along with course fee reimbursements, to support your professional development and ensure success in your university studies.
Why Join the Design Team?
Supportive Team Environment
Our team combines professionalism with a relaxed and supportive culture. We value collaboration, open communication, and the occasional good-natured banter. We pride ourselves on fostering an environment where people can enjoy coming to work and working together to achieve quality outcomes.
Professional Growth and Development
The team provides excellent opportunities for learning and career development. Graduates, cadets and even experienced professionals benefit from mentorship, knowledge sharing and support from highly experienced staff.
Unique Lifestyle Benefits
Based in Cairns, we benefit from the unique lifestyle provided by the area. Nestled between the reef and rainforest, the region offers an abundance of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors and maintain a healthy work-life balance.
Diverse and Meaningful Projects
Our project portfolio is varied and challenging, providing opportunities to work across multiple disciplines and asset types. No two projects are the same, and team members take pride in delivering infrastructure that benefits the local community.
Some benefits we offer:
- Achieve work / life balance with flexible working arrangements
- Fitness Passport - subsidised health and well-being memberships (gym/swimming pool)
- Recharge with up to 5 weeks annual leave
- Up to 3 weeks personal leave
- Cherish family time with up to 14 weeks paid parental leave
- Grow personally and professionally with learning and development opportunities
- Salary sacrifice opportunities
- Up to $5,000 study assistance per annum (inclusive of Fringe Benefits Tax) towards the cost of your Associate Degree in Engineering (Civil)
We are committed to:
- Fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment
- Embracing innovation and continuous improvement
- Cultivating a culture of professional growth and support
Now we want to hear about YOU!
Applications MUST be submitted online through the 'Apply' button and include a Cover Letter addressing the selection criteria and Resume outlining previous academic and work experience and if requested include attachments of the relevant qualifications and licenses, relating to the role.
For further information about this role please download the Position Description which includes the Key Duties, Responsibilities and Selection Criteria.

Phone: (07) 4044 3310
Email: jobs@cairns.qld.gov.au
Website: Employment at Council | Cairns Regional Council

candidates.content_text:
Build infrastructure that keeps Queensland moving!
Are you a civil engineer ready to apply your technical knowledge to meaningful transport projects? Join Transport and Main Roads and help plan, deliver and manage roads, bridges and other infrastructure that support safe and reliable travel across Central Queensland.
About the role
As a Civil Engineer, you will work with experienced engineering and project professionals across the full project lifecycle. You will contribute to transport planning, project development, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management activities, while building your capability under the guidance of senior engineering staff.
Central Queensland Region manages transport infrastructure across more than 600,000 square kilometres, including over 9,000 kilometres of state-controlled roads and 1,500 kilometres of the National Land Transport Network. With offices in Rockhampton, Mackay, Emerald and Barcaldine, the region offers exposure to varied infrastructure, environments and engineering challenges.
In this role, you will:
* provide technical engineering advice and undertake assessments to support planning, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management
* manage projects or project components to achieve quality outcomes, value for money and sound engineering practice
* identify project risks, emerging issues and opportunities, and develop practical and cost-effective solutions
* support procurement activities and the administration of consultant and construction contracts
* coordinate budgets, forecasting, accruals, procurement and performance reporting
* contribute to the delivery of road, bridge, maintenance and asset improvement projects
* build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders
* ensure work meets relevant governance, safety, risk management and departmental requirements.
What you will bring
You will use sound judgement, take responsibility for the quality of your work and collaborate effectively to achieve project outcomes. You will be comfortable applying civil engineering and project management principles across multiple infrastructure projects, while actively developing your professional knowledge and capability.
You must hold:
* a four-year Washington Accord accredited Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering, or an equivalent qualification accepted by Engineers Australia
* a current Class C driver licence.
Why join TMR?
You will gain hands-on experience across diverse transport infrastructure projects while working alongside experienced professionals. TMR supports career development, an inclusive workplace and a healthy work-life balance.
This role provides an opportunity to strengthen your technical, project management, commercial and stakeholder engagement skills while contributing to infrastructure that makes a practical difference for Queensland communities.
If you are looking for varied civil engineering work, professional support and the opportunity to contribute across the full project lifecycle, we encourage you to apply.
Applications to remain current for 12 months.             
Job Ad Reference: QLD/707063/26
Closing Date: Wednesday, 25 November 2026

bullets: Join a Tier 1 Contractor!
Genuine opportunities for progression across the CIMIC Group
Competitive salary package
candidates.content_text:
The UGL Utilities team designs, constructs and maintains critical infrastructure across the water and power sectors. Ranging from wastewater treatment plants to power stations. We design and construct the following assets; power generation, transmission lines, substations, electrical distribution networks, water and wastewater treatment plans and water pipelines.
 Our Utilities team works hard and celebrates successes and efforts. If you are looking for a bright future and opportunity to grow your career, then join UGL – a great place to work!
 The Opportunity
 UGL Utilities team are currently looking for an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join the team in Perth. This role requires DIDO to the project site in Narrogin on a 2:1 roster.  
 Key Responsibilities 
 - Develop and implement detailed project plans, work schedules, and methodologies for civil works, ensuring alignment with project timelines, budgets and scope.
 - Review and interpret technical drawings, specifications, and contracts; provide engineering input to ensure compliance with industry standards, UGL requirements, and client expectations.
 - Oversee on-site civil construction activities, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and to the requires quality standards; manage subcontractor performance and resolve site issues as they arise.
 - Promote and enforce UGL’s HSE policies and procedures across all civil project activities; ensure risk assessments and safety measures are effectively implemented.
 - Liase with clients, internal teams, and external stakeholders to provide regular updates. Manage expectations, and address engineering or construction challenges; prepare and deliver progress reports and technical documentation.
 About you
 - Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline, with eligibility for membership with Engineers Australia (or equivalent).
 - Proven experience delivering civil engineering works in infrastructure, utilities, or construction projects – ideally within a multi-disciplinary or contractor environment.
 - Strong understanding of civil design principles, construction methodologies, and relevant Australian standards, with the ability to interpret drawings and technical documentation.
 - Demonstrated commitment to health, safety, environmental, and quality standards, with experience implementing and maintaining compliance on project sites.
 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with internal teams, client and subcontractors to achieve project outcomes.
 What makes you right for UGL 
 - Ability to provide a safe, supportive, and positive workplace. 
 - Empower a united and collaborative culture.
 - Deliver technical excellence and create efficient, innovative solutions.
 - Build an enviable reputation and the trust of employees, clients, and other stakeholders.
 - Genuine concern for safety.
 About Us   
 UGL is well-known and respected for providing end-to-end engineering, construction and maintenance services within, rai and transport, communications and technology systems, oil and gas, power, renewables and resources, water and defence markets. UGL partners with some of the world’s largest blue-chip companies and government agencies, private enterprises, and public institutions. We are a member of the CIMIC Group of companies.
 At UGL, we value diversity – in the backgrounds, ideas, work styles and perspectives of our team. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and strongly encourage people with disability, Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander people, mature aged workers, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds to apply. 
 Please note that relevant screening checks will be conducted as part of the recruitment process. These may include a national criminal history check and for you to undergo pre-employment medical assessment including drug and alcohol screen. 
 UGL does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or recruitment agencies.

With a proud history of delivering for clients across the infrastructure, resources and marine sectors, we offer our people the opportunity to take ownership, build their capability and contribute to projects that make a lasting impact.
Austral Construction is part of Keller Group plc, the world’s largest geotechnical specialist contractor, giving our people the backing of a global organisation while retaining the hands-on culture and delivery focus that defines Austral.

- Liaise with clients on tender queries, and design, construction and contract issues,
- Brief subcontractors on construction plans and delegate responsibilities,
- Review tender documents and preliminary designs for alternative solutions,
- Prepare cash flow budgets and reconciliations,
- Provide technical advice and solutions ensuring quality control & assurance is maintained for the delivery of works in your area,
- Proactively provide input and support in the maintenance of a safe workplace,
- Manage information and conduct appropriate monitoring and reporting duties.
Position requirements: 
- Preferably a minimum of 3 years’ experience in a similar site-based role with experience in delivery of earthworks projects,
- Tertiary Qualifications in Civil Engineering, Construction Management or a similar field,
- Ability to read and understand drawings and specifications,
- Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills, and a genuine concern for health, safety and the environment,
- Developed analytical and problem-solving skills while adhering to deadlines,
- Team player mindset with the ability to develop strong internal and external relationships,
- Competent in the use of planning software such as MS Project, P6 and Pronto.
What’s on offer: 
- Project Engineering role - preferably Perth-based and willing to undertake a 2:1 FIFO roster arrangement,
- Highly attractive salary + 41% uplift on base salary,
- Exposure to technically challenging projects,
- Opportunities for growth and progression,
Successful candidates will be required to pass a full medical, online tests and inductions.
If this position sounds like the challenging & rewarding role that you have been seeking, please apply and attach a current CV detailing your suitability for the role.
All applicants will be reviewed for shortlisting. Should your application be shortlisted we will contact you.
Austral Construction is committed to building a workplace culture that values diversity and inclusion. We actively promote the employment of people with disabilities, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders, LGBTIQ+ and other diversity groups.

candidates.content_text:
You’ve got a few years of civil design behind you. You can run your own day, and you’re ready for more say in how things come together. This is the next step, without yet being a senior. 
 The firm
 This isn’t a big corporate where you’re a number on a utilisation sheet. It feels boutique, with a lot of industry experience in the room, and that experience is open to you. People know each other, help each other and pull in the same direction. It’s a united company.
 The role
 - Design civil packages from concept through to construction.
 - Work within a strong, collaborative design team.
 - Hand your drafting to a separate drafting team. 
 - Learn from senior engineers who have done this for a long time
 - Take on more ownership of projects and authority relationships as you grow.
 You’ll bring
 - Around three years’ experience in civil design (ideally from a single tenure of employment)
 - A degree in civil engineering.
 - Confidence with design software such as 12D.
 - A practical approach and an interest in improvement.
 The setup
 - An office in Malvern East.
 - Hybrid working, with one to two days a week from home.
 - A culture people stay for.
 The role will pay your worth, which we expect to be around $90k - $108k p/a plus Super.

Tracc Civil is a civil construction and earthmoving contractor based in Bibra Lake, Western Australia, delivering projects across the Perth metropolitan area.

You’ll help teams confirm the scope and quantities, understand the cost implications of updated designs and site requirements, and make timely decisions about upcoming works.
In this dedicated role, you’ll work with Project Managers, Engineers, Supervisors, Procurement and the tender team to understand how work will be delivered and prepare accurate, practical estimates for awarded and live projects.

- Experience pricing civil construction work as an estimator, project engineer, quantity surveyor or contracts administrator.

- Prepare itemised estimates and variation pricing for Project Manager review, supported by marked-up drawings, quantity calculations and clear assumptions.
- Track pricing requests, agree priorities and due dates with project teams, and raise information gaps early.

- Competitive salary based on experience, with weekly pay.
- A permanent, full-time position based in Bibra Lake, with site visits as required.
- Paid training and upskilling, free on-site parking and access to our Employee Assistance Program.
- The opportunity to shape how Tracc Civil provides estimating support to its construction teams.

candidates.content_text:
Pacific Energy is an Australian market leader in the provision of sustainable distributed energy. Our purpose is to transition the world to a clean energy future.
As Australia’s only end-to-end provider of all renewable energy technologies, with proven experience integrating solar, wind, battery energy storage and green hydrogen into new and existing systems, we deliver industry firsts that are leading the clean energy transition.
We are currently seeking 2 x Draftsperson to join our Design & Engineering department. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented professional with a passion for electrical design and drafting to contribute to diverse power generation, renewable energy and infrastructure projects.
As a Draftsperson, you will be responsible for developing and modifying technical drawings, schematics and electrical documentation using industry-leading CAD software. Working closely with engineers and project teams, you will support projects from concept through to commissioning while ensuring all drawings are accurate, compliant and delivered on schedule.
Key Responsibilities
 - Produce accurate and detailed engineering drawings using AutoCAD, MicroStation and other CAD software
 - Develop electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, single line diagrams (SLDs) and associated documentation
 - Convert engineering specifications and design information into high-quality technical drawings
 - Support engineering activities throughout the project lifecycle, from concept design to commissioning
 - Prepare drawings in accordance with client specifications and project requirements
 - Conduct drawing reviews and ensure compliance with quality assurance procedures
 - Liaise with internal stakeholders to incorporate drawing mark-ups and design changes
 - Contribute to drafting standards, technology improvements and continuous improvement initiatives
 - Support Operations & Maintenance activities where required
 - Ensure Safety in Design principles and HSEQ requirements are consistently applied
About You
To be successful in this role, you will possess:
 - Formal drafting qualifications, Certificate IV in Engineering Technology (Electrical), or equivalent experience
 - Minimum 2 years' experience in a drafting or electrical design environment preferred
 - Strong proficiency with CAD software, including AutoCAD and/or MicroStation
 - Experience with Revit and Microsoft Office applications
 - Working knowledge of: 
 - Electrical circuitry and design
 - Loop diagrams
 - Single Line Diagrams (SLDs)
 - Hazardous area drawings
 - Instrumentation and control systems
 - Panel design and PLC hardware
 - Strong understanding of document control processes and standards
 - Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills
 - Strong communication and stakeholder engagement abilities
 - Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality work within deadlines
Why Join Us
We invest in our people and offer benefits designed to support career development, wellbeing and work-life balance, including:
 - Full-time, permanent opportunity with free onsite parking in Kewdale
 - Competitive remuneration package
 - Nine-day fortnight option and flexible working arrangements
 - Health and wellbeing reimbursement
 - Rewards Gateway employee discounts
 - Employee referral bonus program
 - Salary sacrifice options for superannuation, vehicles and education
 - Ongoing training, development and career progression opportunities
Eligibility
To be considered, you must have permanent and unrestricted working rights in Australia.
For more information, visit Pacific Energy Careers.

candidates.content_text:
Ready to take your land development experience to the next level?
Stantec Community Development team is looking for a Construction Engineer to join our Melbourne team, working across a diverse portfolio of land development and subdivision projects .
This is a hands-on role for an engineer who enjoys being close to construction, solving problems on site, working with contractors and clients, and helping projects move successfully from design through to delivery.
What you'll be doing
Working across residential and land development projects, you'll be responsible for:
- Providing contract administration throughout the construction phase
- Preparing, reviewing and managing tender documentation and submissions
- Assessing and managing variations, RFIs and contractor queries
- Undertaking site inspections and construction audits
- Auditing and signing off on water and sewer works and other civil infrastructure
- Identifying and resolving complex engineering and construction issues on site
- Preparing clear, professional engineering and construction reports
- Working closely with developers, contractors, consultants, authorities and other key stakeholders
- Helping ensure works are delivered in accordance with relevant designs, specifications and approval requirements
About you
We're looking for someone with:
- A degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline
- Construction Engineering experience working on land development and subdivision projects
- Strong construction-phase and contract administration experience ideally using AS4000 or AS2124 Australian standard
- Practical knowledge of civil construction, particularly water, sewer and subdivision infrastructure
- Sewer and/or Water audit accreditation like SA1, WA1 and more
- Experience managing RFIs, variations, inspections and contractor interfaces
- Strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to resolve technical issues on site
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
- The ability to balance technical quality, commercial considerations and project delivery
What we offer
We offer many benefits to ensure your professional development & wellbeing is ongoing.
- Genuine Flexible Working Arrangements - Including work from home opportunities, provision for school term contracts, job sharing and part time employment.
- Option to purchase up to 4 weeks additional leave.
- Learning and Talent Development Programs - Including Global programmes, online learning and on-the-job learning
- Professional Memberships, Salary Continuance Insurance (SCI), Service Recognition Awards
- Mental Health, Employee Assistance Program and Wellbeing Programs
About Stantec
The Stantec community unites approximately 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across six continents. We collaborate across disciplines and industries to bring buildings, energy, resources, water, environmental, transport and infrastructure projects to life. Our work from initial project concept and planning through design, construction, and commissioning begins at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships.
Culture
Stantec is serious about healthy work-life balance, diversity, inclusion & equity, indigenous relations, innovation, community engagement, corporate sustainability, and social wellbeing. We have employee groups for women, LGBTQI , neurodiversity, and more! Our employees play sport, fundraise, volunteer, learn, and have fun together.
We are committed to reconciliation and to building respectful relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. We’re better together when different perspectives are welcomed and valued, and we’re committed to a workplace where everyone can belong and thrive. candidates.content_text:
Company description:
Future Generation Joint Venture (FGJV) is the principal contractor for Snowy Hydro's Snowy 2.0, Australia's largest committed renewable energy project. We bring the combined engineering expertise of three companies - Italy's Webuild (formerly Salini Impregilo), Australian-based Clough and US-based Lane Construction.
Snowy 2.0 is the next chapter in the Snowy Scheme's history. It is the largest committed renewable energy project in Australia and will provide on-demand energy and large-scale storage for many generations to come. This Iconic Project has and will continue to create its own legacy in Australian history.
Job description:
 Purpose of the Role
 The Technical Office Engineer works closely with the Senior Technical Office Engineer and a multidisciplinary engineering team to ensure the feasibility, safety, constructability, and compliance of both permanent and temporary works associated with underground construction activities. A key aspect of the role is acting as the technical interface between the Hydromechanical and Electromechanical subcontractors and the Civil Works Department, ensuring effective coordination of design, procurement, installation, and construction activities.
 The role is responsible for coordinating and leading the preparation of technical documentation, engineering deliverables, construction methodologies, and design reviews, while liaising with construction, design, planning, quality, and subcontractor teams to ensure accuracy, completeness, and alignment with project requirements, applicable standards, contractual obligations, and construction objectives.
 Qualifications
 - Tertiary qualification in civil engineering or related discipline
 - White Card
 Experience
 - Minimum 3 years of experience working in an engineering role
 - Experience working in multidisciplinary engineering environments
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering activities across design and construction teams - preferred
 Required Competencies
 - Strong technical understanding of underground, concrete works, and tunnelling methods and best practices
 - Intermediate knowledge of engineering concepts
 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills
 - Basic proficiency in the use of AutoCAD 2D to read drawings
 - Well-developed time management skills
 - Adept to prioritising tasks under pressure and delivering quality work in a fast-paced environment
 - Effective problem-solving capabilities
 - Strong initiative and proactive nature
 - Key collaborative skills
 - High attention to detail
 - Proficiency in the use of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint
 Core Accountabilities and Responsibilities
 - Coordinate technical documentation by gathering, analysing, simplifying, summarising, and providing information.
 - Prepare documentation such as: - Construction method statements,
 - Material approval requests,
 - Scope of works,
 - Technical evaluations,
 - Design change requests,
 - Requests for information,
 - Sketches,
 - Calculations and reports,
 - Risk assessment,
 - Temporary Works design.
 - Liaise with other departments for the development of the above-mentioned documents.
 - Ensure accuracy and completeness of deliverables.
